# Sponsored video review (strict): would the brand approve this creator's script, and is it safe to run?
name: Sponsored video review (strict)
version: "2"
description: Would the brand approve this sponsored script as written, and could it legally run?
context: |
  You review a creator's script for a sponsored video. brief.json is the brand's brief; notes.json is the creator's
  own notes from the month they used the product. Judge only the script text. Be strict: when in doubt, judge it as
  failing. Each check looks only at the kind of problem it names; ignore other kinds of problems when judging it.
language: en
scale: { type: numeric, min: 1, max: 5 }
judges:
  jev: { type: decision, provider: typesafe, model: jev-latest }
  clef: { type: decision, provider: cloudflare, model: "@cf/cloudflare/clef" }
defaultJudge: { type: ref, ref: jev }

criteria:
  # ---------- quality: how many points the script can earn ----------
  - id: audience
    name: Speaks to the brief's audience
    weight: 3
    inputs: [script, brief]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: off, description: "Generic; nothing in it is about renters who split rent and bills" }
      - { value: 3, label: partial, description: "Touches the audience's situation once, but mostly talks to anyone" }
      - { value: 5, label: exact, description: "Speaks to renters who split rent and bills, in situations they have (roommates, shared costs, a tight month)" }
  - id: shown
    name: Shows the product in use
    weight: 2
    inputs: [script, brief]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: told, description: "Praise and adjectives; you can't tell what the app does" }
      - { value: 3, label: some, description: "Names features, but tells more than it shows" }
      - { value: 5, label: shown, description: "Walks through the features in use, each with a concrete number or moment from the month" }
  - id: voice
    name: Sounds like the creator, not ad copy
    weight: 1
    inputs: [script]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: ad_copy, description: "Superlatives and slogans (perfect, changed everything, so much smarter)" }
      - { value: 3, label: mixed, description: "Mostly personal, with some ad-copy lines" }
      - { value: 5, label: personal, description: "Plain first-person talk about what happened, with no slogans or superlatives" }

  # ---------- gate: a claim the brand can't legally make scores 0 ----------
  - id: claims_safe
    name: No claim on the must-not list
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [unsafe, safe] }
    anchors:
      unsafe: "The script makes a claim on the brief's must_not list: credit or loan approval, investment returns or interest, or that Tallyleaf is a bank, holds money or is FDIC-insured"
      safe: "No claim about credit or loan approval, investment returns, interest, banking or FDIC insurance. Other problems are judged elsewhere"

  # ---------- checks: each one passed adds 1/9 of the quality score ----------
  - id: disclosure
    name: Paid relationship disclosed upfront
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, disclosed] }
    anchors:
      missing: "The script doesn't say in plain words, in its first 30 seconds and before the app is shown, that Tallyleaf paid for the video, with 'Paid ad' on screen. A thank-you, a 'friends at', a mention only at the end or only in the description doesn't count"
      disclosed: "In its first 30 seconds, before the app is shown, the script says plainly that Tallyleaf paid for the video and puts 'Paid ad' on screen"
  - id: own_experience
    name: Personal experience matches the creator's notes
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, notes]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [mismatch, matches] }
    anchors:
      mismatch: "The script says the creator used Tallyleaf for longer or more often than notes.json (days_used: 30), or says they did, found or spent something notes.json doesn't contain"
      matches: "How long the creator used Tallyleaf, and everything they say they did, found or spent, is in notes.json. Opinions, and promises to viewers, are judged elsewhere"
  - id: typical_results
    name: Results stay the creator's own
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [promised, own] }
    anchors:
      promised: "The script tells viewers they will save or get a result (a sum, a percentage, 'you'll save'), instead of presenting it as what happened to the creator"
      own: "Every result is presented as the creator's own, with no promise of what viewers will save or get"
  - id: trial_terms
    name: Free-trial terms stated with the offer
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, stated] }
    anchors:
      missing: "The script offers a free trial or free month without saying, where it makes the offer, that it then costs $4.99 a month unless you cancel"
      stated: "Where the script makes the free offer, it says the price after the free month ($4.99 a month) and that you can cancel"
  - id: no_competitor
    name: Names no competitor
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [named, none] }
    anchors:
      named: "The script names another budgeting app or compares Tallyleaf with one"
      none: "No other budgeting app is named or compared"
  - id: talking_points
    name: Covers all three talking points
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, covered] }
    anchors:
      missing: "At least one of the brief's three talking points is missing: automatic categories, the alert the day before a subscription renews, shared budgets"
      covered: "The script covers all three talking points: automatic categories, the alert the day before a subscription renews, and a shared budget"
  - id: call_to_action
    name: Gives the code and where the link is
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, given] }
    anchors:
      missing: "The script doesn't say the code SMALLDESK or doesn't say the link is in the description"
      given: "The script says the code SMALLDESK and that the link is in the description"
  - id: drawback
    name: Names a real drawback
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [script, notes]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, named] }
    anchors:
      missing: "The script names nothing the creator didn't like, or says the app is perfect"
      named: "The script names at least one real drawback from notes.json"

aggregation:
  method: formula
  formula: "claims_safe_n < 0.5 ? 0 : (audience_n * 3 + shown_n * 2 + voice_n) / 6 * (1 + disclosure_n + own_experience_n + typical_results_n + trial_terms_n + no_competitor_n + talking_points_n + call_to_action_n + drawback_n) / 9"
  normalize: [0, 100]
  precision: 0
  gates:
    - { criterion: claims_safe, min: 1, message: "Brand safety: the script makes a claim on the brief's must-not list" }
  grades: [{ label: approve, min: 80 }, { label: revise, min: 50 }, { label: reject, min: 0 }]
  passThreshold: 80
